CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up of chronic problems.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Bruce is a 60-year-old male with past medical history significant for depression, type 2 diabetes, and hypertension presenting for follow-up of chronic problems. He reports it has been a crazy year and a half with anxiety and stress related to preparing for Thanksgiving. He did have a nice holiday seeing family after about two years, though it was a lot of work and stressful. He is planning to take a vacation to somewhere warm for the new year.

Regarding depression, he tried a new strategy over the summer of taking long walks outside every morning during nice weather and working in the yard on weekends. He found this helped with activity and sun exposure. However, with the seasons changing and cold weather, he has not been able to continue this and is looking for new alternatives. He is not ready to try medications and would like to explore alternative options including therapy. He denies any thoughts of harming himself or others.

Regarding diabetes management, he got through Halloween okay but did not stick to his diet much during Thanksgiving week. His sugar intake control is improving and he has been trying to monitor it closely.

Regarding hypertension, he purchased the blood pressure cuff as recommended and readings have been pretty moderate with nothing out of the ordinary.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, abdominal pain, blood in stool, or weight loss.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Depression, type 2 diabetes, hypertension.

MEDICATIONS
Metformin, lisinopril.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recently had holiday gatherings with family. Planning vacation. Enjoys outdoor activities and yard work when weather permits.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure good. Neck exam: No carotid bruits appreciated. Heart exam: Slight 2/6 systolic ejection murmur heard at the left base, previously identified. Lungs: Clear bilaterally. Extremities: 1+ non-pitting edema bilaterally in lower extremities.

RESULTS
EKG: No concerning findings. Hemoglobin A1C: 8 (goal closer to 6).

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Depression: Referral to psychiatry for talk therapy, not medications.
2. Type 2 Diabetes: Increase metformin to 1000 mg twice daily. Order hemoglobin A1C in next couple months. Order lipid panel.
3. Hypertension: Order echocardiogram to recheck heart murmur. Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily.
